githubactions:S7637.name: External GitHub Actions and workflows should be pinned to a commit hash
githubactions:S7637.description:
Referencing an external action by a mutable tag or branch (for example
"@v2" or "@main") lets the action's owner, or anyone who compromises the
action's repository, change the code that runs in this workflow without any
change to the workflow file. Pin every external action to a full-length
commit SHA, and keep the human-readable version in a trailing comment
(for example "# v2.16.0") so it can still be reviewed and updated.

dart:S3776.name: Cognitive Complexity of functions should not be too high
dart:S3776.description:
Cognitive Complexity measures how hard a function's control flow is to
understand. Each break in linear flow (if, else, ternary, loop, catch,
switch, logical-operator sequence) adds to the score, and nesting adds more.
Reduce it by extracting nested parts into well-named private methods or
widgets, using early returns, and flattening nested conditionals, while
keeping behavior unchanged.

dart:S3358.name: Ternary operators should not be nested
dart:S3358.description:
Nested ternary operators (a conditional expression inside another
conditional expression) are hard to read. Extract the inner conditional
into an independent statement, for example an if/else chain or a separate
local variable or helper function, so each decision is stated once.

dart:S7115.name: "mounted" should be checked before using a "BuildContext " after an async operation
dart:S7115.description:
After an await, the widget that owns a BuildContext may have been unmounted,
so the context must not be used without checking that the same context is
still mounted. Checking an unrelated "mounted" (such as State.mounted when a
different BuildContext is used) does not protect the context. Guard each use
after an async gap with "if (!context.mounted) return;" (or
"context.mounted &&") on the exact context being used.

dart:S7055.name: Wildcard variable shouldn't be used
dart:S7055.description:
"_" is a wildcard: since Dart 3.7 it declares no variable and cannot be
referenced. Code that reads a parameter or catch variable named "_" relies
on pre-wildcard behavior. Give the variable a real name (for example "e" or
"error") wherever it is actually used.
